TIPS: Select one of your ships: it has a green ring underneath. Gold hexes show where it can move, and the fans show its firing arcs.
You and the enemy take turns one ship at a time: activate one of yours, then the enemy activates one of theirs, until every ship has acted. Then a new round starts.

Hover a gold hex to preview the move: the ghost shows where you will end up and which way you will face. Q and E turn in place. Moving matters: a ship that ends its activation in the same hex is easier to hit (enemies get +10), and turning in place does not count. Moving 3 or more hexes makes it harder to hit (−5). Bracing cancels the sitting-still penalty. Some factions bend these numbers; the ship panel shows each ship's own.

The cyan bars on the ship panel are its shields: four facings that soak hits and recharge each turn. The shield bubble itself glows in its faction's colour. Amber is hull: damage that stays. Keep your strongest shield facing the enemy.
Enemies you can hit have a pulsing red ring. Hover one for hit odds and expected damage, then click to fire every weapon that bears. Keys 1 to 6 pick a single weapon.
Each ship acts once per round. When this ship is done, press End activation (Enter) and the enemy moves one of theirs.
Your admiral's signature move is ready: it glows gold on the strip. You get it once per battle. It grows each round you wait and when you lose a ship, so pick your moment.
Ramming speed (X) charges the first enemy dead ahead. Boarding (G) sends crews into an adjacent enemy; win and the ship is yours.
Before you end a move, check where the enemy can reach. Press R, or Threat in the top bar, to shade every hex their guns can hit next turn: the darker the hex, the more damage is waiting there.
Not every fight is a slugging match. The top bar shows this fight’s goal; tap the map chip under it for the full rules and what the coloured hexes mean.
